sections.title: He knows the system *inside and out*
body: Before opening The Chandler Law Firm, Everett K. Chandler worked for six years in the Second Judicial Circuit Solicitor’s Office in Aiken County. Over the years he has worked on a large number of criminal cases and learned what to expect, and what it takes.

Whether you face a DUI, a drug charge, a felony or a misdemeanor, have been hurt on the job, or need to recover losses from an accident, you can expect complete dedication to your case and thorough preparation for every hearing and trial.
list: Downtown Aiken office on Waterloo Street

items.title: Call before you talk
items.text: Even at the “talking” stage with police or investigators, it matters to have a lawyer.

items.title: Act on deadlines
items.text: After a DUI arrest you have a limited time to request a hearing, and injury claims have time limits too.

items.title: Preserve evidence
items.text: Photos, witnesses and reports are gathered from the moment you hire us.

items.title: Plan your defense
items.text: We review legal and factual defenses and prepare thoroughly for court.

items.q: Can I lose my license before a DUI conviction?
items.a: Yes. In South Carolina, a DUI/DUAC arrest can suspend your license automatically depending on your blood alcohol level, and you have a limited time to request an administrative hearing.

items.q: Do I have to prove my employer was negligent for workers’ comp?
items.a: No. For a workers’ compensation claim you only need to show the injury was work-related.
